section_1.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
section_1.content: Introduce Ax=b as the intersection of hyperplanes. Visualize the system as constraints in space. Prerequisite: Basic understanding of vectors as coordinate points.
section_1.example: A robot arm with two joints: each linear equation represents a constraint on an angle; their intersection is the specific pose of the arm.

section_2.title: The Inverse Matrix: Unpacking the Transformation
section_2.content: View the matrix A as a transformation grid. The inverse A⁻¹ is the 'undo' button. Explain that if a system is flattened (determinant 0), it cannot be undone.
section_2.example: A photo-editing tool: Matrix A scales and rotates an image; A⁻¹ acts as the 'Reset' button that returns pixels to their original coordinates.

section_3.title: Column Space: The 'Reachable' World
section_3.content: Define Column Space as the span of the columns of A. Visually, it is the set of all possible output vectors b that the transformation can 'land on'.
section_3.example: A cat moving in a 2D room: If the cat can only move along a specific diagonal plank, the column space is just that 1D line, regardless of how large the room is.

section_4.title: Null Space: The 'Hidden' Kernel
section_4.content: Define Null Space as the set of vectors x where Ax = 0. Visually, these are the directions that get 'squashed' into the origin.
section_4.example: A security camera projection: Any movement of a person along the line of sight of the lens results in no change in the image (the projection is 0); that line of sight is the Null Space.

section_5.title: Synthesizing the Big Picture
section_5.content: Connect the concepts: If the Null Space contains only the zero vector, the transformation is invertible, and every point is reachable.
section_5.example: A 3D printer: The 'Column Space' is the printable volume; the 'Null Space' represents design flaws where multiple distinct parts compress into the same coordinate, causing print failure.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map to right side of screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 1.8 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear equations define constraints in our spatial world.",
            "Imagine a robot arm constrained by these equations.",
            "The intersection of these constraints identifies a pose."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems", lecture_lines)
        
        # Axis and setup
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        self.add(axes)
        
        v1 = Vector([2, 1], color="#FF5733")
        v2 = Vector([1, 2], color="#FF5733")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            ORIGIN, v1.get_end(), v1.get_end() + v2.get_end(), v2.get_end(),
            fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#33FF57", stroke_width=0
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(parallelogram))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF33")
        equation = MathTex(r"c_1v_1 + c_2v_2 = b").set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        
        # Add b vector
        b = Vector([3, 3], color="#33FFFF")
        self.play(Create(b))
        
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # 6x6 grid on the right side of the screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
